question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -1}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x-3}{{x}^{2}-1} & =\frac{(-1)^{2}-2(-1)-3}{(-1)^{2}-1}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x-3}{{x}^{2}-1} & =\frac{(x+1)(x-3)}{(x-1)(x+1)} \\  & =\frac{x-3}{x-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -1}\frac{{x}^{2}-2x-3}{{x}^{2}-1} & ={lim}_{x\to -1}\frac{x-3}{x-1} \\  & =\frac{-1-3}{-1-1} \\  & =\frac{-4}{-2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
